issues.legal_issue: Mere membership in an unlawful assembly formed to commit cattle trespass and forcibly prevent the watchmen from impounding cattle does not establish shared liability for murder when the other members’ knowledge of the fatal weapon’s use is unproved.
material_facts: The accused shepherds formed an unlawful assembly to graze cattle in a field and prevent the watchmen from carrying out their duties by force.
One accused took a sharp weapon from a watchman and used it to strike the victim’s head.
The sequence of the assault was uncertain, and the evidence did not establish that the other accused knew the weapon would be used in that manner.
The stick blows inflicted by the other accused were not aimed at the victim’s head.
issues.conclusion: The acquittal of the other accused of murder liability through the unlawful assembly was correctly affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 149 and 302 of the Indian Penal Code, murder liability through membership in an unlawful assembly requires a basis for attributing the murder to the assembly’s common object or to an offence its members knew was likely to be committed in pursuing that object. The assembly’s non-lethal object, the uncertainty about the sequence of events, the absence of proof that the other members knew how the sharp weapon would be used, and the direction of their blows did not establish that basis. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: state_appeal_from_murder_acquittal and assembly_object_was_trespass_and_forceful_obstruction and weapon_taken_from_companion and other_members_not_shown_to_know_weapon_use and stick_blows_not_aimed_at_head and assault_sequence_uncertain

predicates.state_appeal_from_murder_acquittal: The prosecution appealed an acquittal on a murder charge based on alleged membership in an unlawful assembly.
predicates.assembly_object_was_trespass_and_forcefu: The assembly formed to commit a property trespass and use force to prevent people from carrying out their duties.
predicates.weapon_taken_from_companion: One participant took a sharp weapon from another person during the incident.
predicates.other_members_not_shown_to_know_weapon_u: The evidence did not show that the other participants knew the weapon would be used to inflict the fatal injuries.
predicates.stick_blows_not_aimed_at_head: The other participants’ stick blows were not directed at the victim’s head.
predicates.assault_sequence_uncertain: The evidence did not establish the precise sequence in which the participants took part in the assault.

issues.definition: When a prosecution appeal follows a murder acquittal and the assembly’s object was non-lethal, the weapon’s use was not shown to be known to the other participants, and the assault evidence does not otherwise connect them to the fatal attack, shared murder liability is not established.

issues.legal_issue: An intentional infliction of an injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death constitutes murder even if the accused did not intend to cause death.
material_facts: An accused took a sharp weapon from a watchman and struck the victim on the head three times.
The victim sustained serious head injuries, including a fractured skull, and died that evening.
The medical evidence was consistent with the eyewitness account that the accused inflicted the weapon blows.
The injuries were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
issues.conclusion: The accused’s offence fell under the murder provision, rather than culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and his conviction was altered accordingly.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the third clause of Section 300 of the Indian Penal Code: an intentional infliction of an injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death falls within murder, even where the accused did not intend to cause death. The conviction and punishment were therefore under Section 302 rather than Section 304 Part II. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.state_appeal_challenging_homicide_classi: The prosecution appealed a ruling that treated a fatal assault as culpable homicide rather than murder.
predicates.accused_intentionally_inflicted_head_inj: The accused deliberately struck the victim’s head with a weapon.
predicates.injury_sufficient_to_cause_death_in_ordi: The injury inflicted was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
predicates.medical_evidence_supported_account: The medical evidence was consistent with the account of how the accused inflicted the injury.

issues.definition: If a prosecution appeal challenges a lesser homicide classification and the accused intentionally inflicted an injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, the offence is murder.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent factual findings supporting convictions for trespass, unlawful entry under local law, and causing hurt should not be disturbed when the appellate court finds no reason to differ from them.
material_facts: The trial court and High Court found that the accused grazed cattle in a field and damaged its crop.
Both courts rejected the defence that the field’s owner had permitted the grazing.
The High Court accepted eyewitness evidence and found that the accused were the aggressors.
The Supreme Court found no reason to differ from the concurrent findings supporting the convictions and dismissed the accused’s appeal.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and sentences challenged by the accused were affirmed, subject to the separate alteration of one accused’s homicide conviction in the State’s appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the concurrent factual findings of the trial court and High Court on the evidence and stated that it found no reason to differ from them. It therefore left undisturbed the convictions under Sections 323 and 447 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 162(2) of the Gujarat Panchayats Act. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: accused_appeal_from_conviction and concurrent_courts_found_unauthorized_grazing_and_crop_damage and permission_defence_rejected and eyewitness_evidence_supported_findings and supreme_court_found_no_reason_to_differ

predicates.accused_appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed convictions entered by the lower courts.
predicates.concurrent_courts_found_unauthorized_gra: The trial and appellate courts found that the accused grazed animals without permission and damaged a crop.
predicates.permission_defence_rejected: The lower courts rejected the claim that the property owner had permitted the conduct.
predicates.eyewitness_evidence_supported_findings: The lower courts relied on eyewitness testimony supporting their findings about the incident.
predicates.supreme_court_found_no_reason_to_differ: The Supreme Court found no reason to depart from the lower courts’ concurrent factual findings.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction supported by concurrent findings based on eyewitness evidence, the permission defence has been rejected, and the reviewing court finds no reason to differ, the challenged convictions and sentences are affirmed.
